teaser: Selectmen backed a look at two Town Hall car chargers, heard a new skating-rink site on Profile Road, and returned to weekly meetings.

sections.title: The last week
sections.lead: Selectmen met Monday, September 28, at 4:00 p.m. The minutes are marked draft. They heard a new site for the community skating rink, backed a first look at electric-vehicle chargers at Town Hall, and decided to meet every week.

decided.text: The board approved the September 14 minutes as written and the transaction list for September 25 through October 1. It signed an intent to cut for the Profile Club, map 10 lot 3; a driveway permit for Sperrazza on Oaks Road, map 4 lot 14; and the MS-1.

The board supported moving ahead with Level 2 chargers at the Town Hall and Welcome Center parking lot and authorized Daniel Zajic to contact electrician Justin Poulton. The minutes put the cost at about $5,000 to $10,000, depending on the electrical work, and say he suggested starting with two spaces. This was not a vote to spend the money.
The board decided to resume weekly meetings. The next meeting is Monday, October 5.

comingUp.text: Jennifer Opalinski said the skating rink is now proposed for 1476 Profile Road, about 3.06 acres near Lovett's. It remains under the existing $475,000 grant, and an amendment is being pursued for the new location. She said the site will need a variance and then Planning Board and Zoning Board review.

The agenda scheduled a non-public session at the end of the meeting for reputation. The minutes say the board entered that session at 5:02 p.m. and adjourned when it ended at 5:35 p.m. They do not say what was discussed.

sections.title: The last month
sections.lead: The September 14 meeting ordered a survey of a Mittersill right-of-way, accepted parking-lot and furnace quotes, and heard that Franconia's ambulance contract with Littleton runs out at the end of December.

decided.text: Chair Walker moved to have a survey done to reestablish the right-of-way David Whittemore described at Mittersill. Selectman Meth seconded. The vote was unanimous. Residents also described ice from roof runoff and cars being ticketed. Those comments are in the minutes and were not separate votes.

The board accepted Supreme Seal Coating's quotes, totaling $11,976, to seal the Town Hall and Safety Services parking lots and paint the lines. The money comes from the Town Buildings and Grounds Maintenance Fund. The minutes say Mitchell Seal Coating was slightly lower and did not include the lines. The vote was unanimous.
The board accepted a quote from Tempest Heating and Construction for $6,409.70 to replace the highway garage office furnace, from the same maintenance fund. The vote was unanimous.

The board approved the August 24 minutes as amended and the September 11–17 transaction list. It signed land-use change taxes for the Robert Soucy Trust, map 3 lot 5, and for Ferguson, map 22 lot 4-5, and approved a sign permit for the Franconia Trading Post.

On September 28 the board returned to weekly meetings, authorized a first conversation with an electrician about two Level 2 chargers at Town Hall, and signed the Profile Club intent to cut, the Sperrazza driveway permit, and the MS-1. Those minutes are marked draft.

comingUp.text: Chief Chad Miller said Franconia's EMS contract expires at the end of December and that he will work with Town Administrator Staples on the gap before town meeting. He said a short-term arrangement will be part of the contract brought to town meeting. He also said he feels fairly confident the contract will not increase and may go down. That is his statement, not a vote. He reported Littleton responses in Franconia of 232 in 2023, 283 in 2024, 231 in 2025, and 274 in the last 12 months, including 102 from Lafayette Center and 45 from the state park, excluding hiking trails and including Artists Bluff.

The next Selectmen's meeting after September 28 is Monday, October 5. The skating-rink site at 1476 Profile Road still needs a variance and Planning Board and Zoning Board review, according to the September 28 minutes.

deadlines.text: Franconia's ambulance contract with Littleton expires at the end of December 2026. Chief Miller also said Littleton EMS received a $40,000 planning grant through the Foundation for Healthy Communities Rural Health Transformation Program, with part of it for studying regional EMS.

sections.title: Year to date
sections.lead: The year still rests on the March 10 town budget and the Littleton ambulance contract. Since then the Planning Board has held a hearing on the Franconia Inn solar array without recording an approval, and the Selectmen have taken up the rink, the chargers, and the Mittersill right-of-way.

decided.text: Town Meeting on March 10 passed a $2,302,440 town budget unanimously and adopted the official zoning map, 107 to 1. The warrant says the map clarifies district boundaries and does not change them. The file is marked for review because the archive date is year only. The March 10 date is in the text.
Article 10 appropriated $607,200 for ambulance service through December 31, 2026, continuing the Littleton contract. It passed unanimously.

On August 25 the Planning Board accepted the Franconia Inn solar site-plan application as complete and held a public hearing. No abutters were present and there were no public comments. The minutes do not record a vote to approve the project.
On September 14 the Selectmen voted to survey the Mittersill right-of-way, accepted $11,976 in seal-coating quotes, and accepted a $6,409.70 furnace quote for the highway garage office.
Energy Commission minutes for August 25 are posted. No text from that file is in this edition, so the meeting is not summarized.

comingUp.text: Because of the state primary on Tuesday, September 8, the Planning Board set its next meeting for Tuesday, September 29.
Selectmen meet next on Monday, October 5. The skating-rink proposal still needs a variance and land-use review.

deadlines.text: The Littleton ambulance contract funded at Town Meeting runs through December 31, 2026, and Chief Miller told the Selectmen on September 14 that Franconia's contract expires at the end of December.
Energy Commission minutes say the IRA program ends December 31, 2026.
